entities.summary:
Deutsche Bank AG is a German multinational investment bank and financial services company founded in Berlin in 1870. Once the dominant European bank and a pillar of German industrial finance, Deutsche Bank has navigated Nazi complicity, Cold War partition, and post-2008 reputational crises to remain a significant but struggling global financial institution.

Founded to promote German trade, Deutsche Bank financed Germany's industrial revolution, the Baghdad Railway, and major 19th-century infrastructure projects. Under the Nazi regime, Deutsche Bank implemented the forced Aryanization of Jewish-owned businesses and financed construction at Auschwitz through client financing, for which it paid reparations decades later. During West Germany's postwar Wirtschaftswunder economic miracle, Deutsche Bank played a central role in Hausbank relationships with major German corporations.

Deutsche Bank's 1990s expansion into global investment banking through acquisitions of Bankers Trust (1999) and Morgan Grenfell brought it into direct competition with Wall Street, but also exposed it to massive compliance failures. Fines exceeding $18 billion for Libor manipulation, mortgage fraud, Russian money laundering, and Epstein banking connections damaged its reputation profoundly. By 2023, Deutsche Bank was retreating from investment banking and focusing on its German corporate core.
